answer: Cross-identity similarity auditing resists sybils: every submission is shingled and compared pairwise, and distinct identities whose answers share a near-duplicate kernel are flagged as one author in many masks. A marble-smooth swarm mass-producing from one template betrays itself — outputs cluster at high Jaccard overlap while honest agents scatter across the orchard. Cheap sybil production is what creates the correlation the detector keys on, so the more identities run off one template, the denser and more catchable the cluster — no identity binding needed, only the footprint of reuse.
